---
name: make-music
description: "Compose or revise music, critique mixes against references, and find local samples."
applications:
  - id: ableton
    role: alternative
  - id: logic-pro
    role: alternative
  - id: moda
    role: alternative
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: none
---

A beat or part in the user's Ableton Live set follows `ableton-live`. You cannot hear; the user judges by ear.

## Route

Engine commands below are subcommands of the audio engine's CLI that `<voyager_environment>` names.

- Compose in Voyager's audio engine by default when `<voyager_environment>` lists it as ready, video scores included.
- Tweaks ("punchier", "darker", "slower", "less busy", "longer intro"): keep editing the same .vdaw.
- When you composed in the engine, link its .vdaw project in your reply beside the audio, so the user can open it.
- Generate without an engine draft for vocals or lyrics, realistic acoustic or orchestral sound, when the user asks for AI generation or names a provider, and when the audio engine is not ready.
- To change a generated track, split it into stems in an engine project (`track separate FILE`: vocals, drums, bass and other) and edit those instead of regenerating.
- For lyric timings from an existing song, use `voyager speech transcribe FILE --local --no-vad --accurate --output DIR`, adding `--language CODE` when known. The speech detector can discard singing; review the returned words and timings against the lyrics (see [speech edits](../edit-video/references/speech-edits.md)).

## Critique a track or mix

Requires the audio engine to be ready in `<voyager_environment>`. Report measurements, not a verdict on taste. Without references, `--profile NAME` (`library reference profile list`) gives only a rough genre baseline.

```sh
analyze compare references BOUNCE.wav --reference REF.wav --reference REF2.wav
analyze compare references BOUNCE.wav --reference REFS_DIR --range drop
analyze compare diff --previous OLD.wav NEW.wav
```

For requested changes to an Ableton set, use [ableton-live](../ableton-live/SKILL.md).

## Find local samples

Requires the audio engine to be ready in `<voyager_environment>`. Register sample folders once, then index:

```sh
library path add ~/Splice
library index --no-plugins
```

`sound find --source sample --class snare --want punchy,tight --key "F#m" --folder DIR` searches by sound. `--reference FILE` ranks by similarity; `--more` and `--less` describe changes relative to it. `sound classes` and `sound descriptors` list valid values.

`kit add --name NAME --want dusty,warm --folder DIR` builds a kit from the library. Import picks into a .vdaw with `import audio FILE --track NAME`; for an Ableton set, use [ableton-live](../ableton-live/SKILL.md). For recorded sounds missing from the library, see [Freesound](../make-sound/SKILL.md#sound-effects).

## Generate

When the user explicitly chooses another tool or website, such as Suno on their own custom connector, generate there instead of the credit check and `eleven-music` below; the other rules here still apply.

Otherwise estimate first (`voyager models estimate eleven-music --prompt "..." --count N --json`). `eleven-music` uses the user's connected ElevenLabs key before Voyager credits by default (the provider order controls routing) and needs no Voyager plan on that key. Fal's `elevenlabs/music/v2.5` and `fal-ai/elevenlabs/music` use a different route; choose `eleven-music` for the user's ElevenLabs account. For Music v2.5 on their key, set `parameters.model_id` to `music_v2_5` in both the estimate and run; version selection runs only on the own-key route. Without it, `music_v1` runs on either route. On `no_paying_route`, or `short` with no Voyager plan, say in one line that this shortcut needs Voyager credits or the user's own ElevenLabs key (Connectors → Providers), submit nothing, and offer the audio engine when it is ready and can do the job.

Generate with `eleven-music` through `voyager`: `voyager models run --input - --json` with `{"model": "eleven-music", "prompt": "…", "parameters": {"duration": 10, "instrumental": true}}` (a video's bed is instrumental, the picture's length). Never ask for a particular song's melody or hook. Before generating, read the model's section in [audio and image prompting](../choose-media-model/references/audio-image-prompting.md#music). Another music model only when the user names one or needs what Eleven Music lacks ([choose-media-model](../choose-media-model/SKILL.md)). A refused generation of music the user asked for is a [billing wall](../choose-media-model/SKILL.md#billing-walls). A default bed they didn't ask for never stops the piece: on a billing wall, deliver without it and say so in one line.

## Score a video

- With the voiceover in hand, bring it into the score (`import audio VO.wav --track vo`) and duck the music under it there (`bus duck --on BUS --from vo`).
- A generated bed: write the reveal and logo times into the prompt or composition plan as section changes ("open up at 0:12, end on a clean button at 0:30"). Timing is approximate (the job's `audioLength` gives the real length): then shift, trim and fade the bed in the mix so the hit lands on the reveal and the ending lands on the last frame.

Sound effects, the final mix and delivery: [make-sound](../make-sound/SKILL.md#mix-to-the-destination).

## Logic Pro

Logic has no scripting API: write parts as MIDI files and work Logic's menus with computer control.

- A new project: `open -a "Logic Pro" part.mid`, with no file dialog.
- A part for an open project: File > Import > MIDI File, typing the path after Cmd+Shift+G. Never open the browser's All Files tab; it can hang Logic.
- Give every melodic channel a program change so it lands on a software instrument. Channel-10 drums always land on a silent External MIDI track: move the region onto a software instrument track with a drum kit.
- Before a bounce, turn the metronome off (Logic bounces the click), choose WAVE and set the range to the music.

## Asset Sources

For licences, receipts and credits of third-party assets, and where free game art, icons, palettes, plugins and animations come from.

- Each grabbed asset gets a receipt `<asset-id>.json` beside its files (`source`, `id`, `title`, `url`, `authors`, `license`, `licenseUrl`, `attribution`, `acquiredAt`, `files`) and a line in the project's `CREDITS`: title, author, source URL, licence.

- `voyager assets search <words> [--type texture|hdri|model|icon|music|pack] [--source …]` searches Poly Haven (CC0 textures, HDRIs, models), ambientCG (CC0 materials, HDRIs), Kenney (CC0 packs), game-icons.net and Incompetech; `voyager assets download <source>:<id> [--resolution 2k]` saves under `assets/<source>/<id>/` with the receipt and the `CREDITS` line. Poly Haven asks that users are told its assets come from Poly Haven.

- Kenney (kenney.nl): CC0 whole packs (2D, 3D, UI, audio, textures); search matches pack names and categories only. Packs include `License.txt`.

- game-icons.net: CC BY 3.0 (a few authors CC0), credited per icon's author. Each SVG is a black square path under a white icon path; recolour or drop them via `fill`.

- Incompetech: Kevin MacLeod's music, CC BY 4.0 with his credit text; fetch single tracks only.

- Lospec: `https://lospec.com/palette-list/<slug>.json` returns name, author (sometimes empty; the palette page names the creator) and hex colours. Credit "<palette> by <author> (Lospec)".

- Godot Asset Library: keyless JSON at `godotengine.org/asset-library/api/asset?filter=…&godot_version=4.3` (without `godot_version` it returns nothing); `cost` holds the licence, `/asset/<id>` gives `download_url`. Plugins and scripts, not art. The new Godot Asset Store (beta, no public API) is replacing it.

- OpenGameArt: no API. Search pages (`/art-search-advanced?keys=…`) only; robots.txt sets a 10 s crawl delay and disallows `/search/`. Licences (often several, including SA and GPL) and the attribution text are on each content page.

- Mixamo: Adobe's terms forbid access other than through its interface and any data mining, so the user downloads in their own browser; Voyager imports and rigs the FBX. Raw characters and animations are not redistributable.

- itch.io: no search API (every endpoint needs auth and covers your own account); tag pages have RSS (`itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-<tag>.xml`) without licences. Licences are free text per page; the user downloads, and pays where needed.

## Audio Tool Choice

For choosing an audio editor, mixing workflow and paid generation route.

- When `<voyager_environment>` lists Voyager's audio engine as ready, it
  composes music by default, video scores included; `make-music` says when to
  generate instead. Revisions of music it composed edit that same .vdaw in
  place (its history keeps the earlier version); render each revision to a new
  versioned WAV. It is not used for sound effects (whooshes, hits, risers, UI
  clicks, ticks, or a tone or sonic cue under a motion piece or logo sting),
  voice cleanup, or cutting or fitting a whole existing or generated track.

- Sound effects are generated through `voyager` (ElevenLabs sound effects, as
  `make-sound` describes), and cleanup, mixing, fitting, loudness and delivery
  use the bundled FFmpeg or Python audio libraries.

- To start audio late in raw FFmpeg, insert silent samples with
  `adelay=delays=9500:all=1` (milliseconds; an `S` suffix means samples;
  without `all=1` only the first channel moves). Before
  delivering, check the decoded length and where the leading silence ends
  (`silencedetect=n=-50dB:d=0.1`).
